title: Cold rebuild: amend, then revert
summary: Fix the last commit and undo a pushed one in a real repo, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *revert and amend* you fixed an unpushed commit with **amend** and undid a pushed one
with **revert**, in a real repository. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to
peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A bad commit was merged to `main` and pushed an hour ago. Five teammates have pulled since. What is the right way to undo it?
options: `git revert <hash>` and push the new commit
Delete the branch and recreate it
steps.explain: Reset plus force-push would rewrite history everyone already has: their next pull becomes a tangle and the bad commit can sneak back in. Revert adds an undo commit that everyone can simply pull.

steps.title: Amend, then revert, cold
prompt: `~/shop` is pushed up to `Log checkout errors`; the newest commit, `Fix typo in READNE`, is not pushed.
1. Fix the typo in that commit's message and add the forgotten `CHANGELOG.md` to it.
2. Undo the pushed commit `Enable experimental cache` without rewriting pushed history, with Git's default message.
From memory: no hints this time. Finish with a clean `git status`.
